title: An Effective Transition-based Model for Discontinuous NER

bibliographic_context.metadata_policy: Frozen local S01 entry only; no network metadata enrichment.

research_question: Can a neural transition-based parser recognize discontinuous and overlapping biomedical entity mentions while retaining performance on continuous mentions?
methodology: The model reads sentence tokens through a buffer and stores partially built spans on a stack. SHIFT and OUT consume tokens; COMPLETE emits the top span; REDUCE joins the top two spans; LEFT-REDUCE and RIGHT-REDUCE also retain one operand for shared mention components. Token encoding combines word and character-CNN inputs, a bidirectional LSTM, and frozen ELMo features. Stack-LSTM encodes spans; a composition function combines reduced spans. Multiplicative attention relates stack spans to future buffer tokens. The top three spans, their attended buffer representations, and an LSTM representation of action history feed a softmax action selector restricted to valid actions. Evaluation uses strict micro mention precision, recall, and F1 on CADEC ADE and ShARe 13/14 Disorder annotations, with separate full-test, discontinuous-containing-sentence, discontinuous-only, and development-category analyses.

key_findings.finding: Gold biomedical mentions can contain separated components and share a component with another mention; the model predicts such structures in sentence text. The evaluated entity inventory is ADE only on CADEC and Disorder only on each ShARe dataset.
key_findings.quote: The first example contains a discontinuous mention ‘left atrium dilated’, the second example contains two mentions that overlap: ‘muscle pain’ and ‘muscle fa- tigue’ (discontinuous).
key_findings.qualification: Gold shared membership is not merely a label-set capability. Predicted examples and Table 4 establish some overlap recovery, not arbitrary overlap or multiple entity types per identical span.

key_findings.finding: The authors state that action sequences decode unambiguously. The mechanism combines the top two stack spans and can retain one operand for reuse. This one-way decoding claim does not establish that every gold overlap structure has an action encoding.
key_findings.quote: That is, the output sequence of actions can always be unambiguously decoded into mention outputs.
key_findings.section: PDF page 3; Prior Work, comparison of intermediate representations
key_findings.qualification: Design property stated and illustrated; no formal completeness proof, oracle representability rate, or exhaustive overlap-coverage test is reported. See topic02.interpretation for the representation limitation.

key_findings.finding: On full-test strict micro mention evaluation, Ours reports P/R/F1 of 68.9/69.0/69.0 on CADEC ADE, 80.5/75.0/77.7 on ShARe 13 Disorder, and 78.1/81.2/79.6 on ShARe 14 Disorder. Recall and F1 exceed the comparison rows reported for each dataset; Graph has higher precision.

key_findings.qualification: Percent-scale scores for biomedical mention extraction, not Topic identification. No confidence intervals, seed variance, or significance test is reported. Prior-literature rows are cited results, not all rerun baselines.

key_findings.finding: The test subset of sentences containing a gold discontinuous mention still includes continuous mentions. Ours F1 on that subset is 65.4/62.9/63.1 for CADEC/ShARe 13/ShARe 14, whereas discontinuous-mention-only F1 is 37.9/52.5/49.2. Flat scores 42.4/34.2/36.0 on the sentence subset but 0 on discontinuous mentions only.
key_findings.quote: Note that sentences in the former setting usually con- tain continuous mentions as well, including those involved in overlapping structure (e.g., ‘muscle pain’ in the sentence ‘muscle pain and fatigue’).
key_findings.section: PDF page 6; Experimental Results, discontinuous evaluation settings
key_findings.qualification: Dataset order is fixed above; each score is strict micro mention F1 on the named test population. Test gold/prediction counts are not supplied. BIO E. CADEC F1 is 57.3 on the sentence subset and 1.8 on discontinuous mentions only; these are different denominators.

key_findings.finding: Development-set overlap performance varies by category. On no-overlap discontinuous mentions, Ours F1 is 0.0/36.1/57.1 for CADEC/ShARe 13/ShARe 14. It wins left-overlap F1 on CADEC and ShARe 14, while Graph wins left-overlap on ShARe 13 and right-overlap on CADEC and ShARe 13; all right-overlap scores are zero on ShARe 14.

supporting_evidence.section: Table 4, category counts and all F1 scores

key_findings.qualification: All category results are development-only discontinuous NER. See topic02.metrics.table4 for gold counts and all model values; small categories do not justify generalization to work text.

key_findings.finding: Multi-overlap discontinuous-mention F1 is 0.0 for all three evaluated models on CADEC development data (15 gold mentions) and ShARe 14 development data (6 gold mentions). ShARe 13 development data has 0 gold mentions and reports a dash, not a measured zero. The crossing-composition example also shows missed combinations and a false standalone Stiffness prediction.
key_findings.qualification: Empirical failure on evaluated categories; not a negative evaluation of the absent ShARe 13 category. The example is qualitative and its individual split is not explicitly labeled. It does not isolate representational, search, and learning errors.

key_findings.finding: Table 1 headline gold discontinuous-mention totals (CADEC 675; ShARe 13 1,090; ShARe 14 1,710) conflict with both the component-count sums and the overlap-category sums (679; 1,088; 1,650, respectively). These are unresolved source-internal count discrepancies.
key_findings.section: PDF page 5; Table 1, headline discontinuous count
key_findings.qualification: The contradicted claim is the headline total as a consistent total of its stated categories. Sums are analyst arithmetic, not substitute paper totals. Original PDF and independent text extractions agree on the printed values; no denominator is silently corrected.

key_findings.finding: The Flat baseline expands each discontinuous training mention to its shortest covering span and merges overlapping training mentions. Development and test annotations remain unchanged, so Flat is tested against original complex mention targets.
key_findings.quote: we apply these changes only on the training set, but not on the development set and the test set.
key_findings.section: PDF page 6; Baseline Models, Flat model
key_findings.qualification: This transformation changes training boundaries and shared memberships. It is not an experiment showing that covering-span expansion preserves conditions or work-matter identity.

key_findings.finding: A source gold example selects left atrium and dilated while omitting is mildly. The authors also describe inconsistent treatment of severity indicators in CADEC and offer sparsity and annotation practice as explanations for no-overlap errors; these explanations are not independently quantified.
key_findings.quote: severity indicators are annotated as the interval of the discontinuous mention sometimes, but not of- ten.
key_findings.section: PDF page 8; Impact of Overlapping Structure

supporting_evidence.section: Characteristics of Discontinuous Mentions, no overlap

key_findings.qualification: The selected gold spans are observed evidence. The causal explanation is an author hypothesis. Loss of a decision-bearing modifier in msgloom is an analyst transfer risk, not a measured work-text error rate.

key_findings.finding: Development-set recall generally decreases with mention length, while interval-length effects are nonmonotonic. Figure 4 includes continuous mentions in the zero-interval bin and shows Ours competitive on those bins; it is not a separate continuous-only full-test F1 or a noninferiority test against Flat.
key_findings.quote: We found that the recall of all models decreases with the increase of mention length in general (Figure 4 (a – c)),
key_findings.section: PDF page 8; Impact of Mention and Interval Length, Figure 4
key_findings.qualification: Recall coordinates are plotted without exact numeric point labels. No pixel-derived recall values are presented. The proposed annotation explanation for short-interval difficulty remains a hypothesis.

key_findings.finding: The paper motivates discontinuous mention extraction as more useful than separate components for pharmacovigilance and summarization, but it does not evaluate those downstream benefits or preservation of decision-bearing conditions, evidence, approval, action, or reply scope.
key_findings.quote: We argue that, in downstream ap- plications such as pharmacovigilance and summa- rization, recognizing these discontinuous mentions that refer to disorders or symptoms is more useful than recognizing separate components which may refer to body locations or general feelings.
key_findings.qualification: No downstream or work-text preservation evaluation is reported; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of a negative downstream result.

key_findings.finding: The authors say their fine-tuned BERT variant performed worse than the frozen-ELMo feature variant, but supply no dataset-specific numbers or comparison protocol for that experiment.
key_findings.quote: However, this fine- tuning approach with BERT does not achieve as good performance as feature extraction approach with ELMo (Peters et al., 2019).
key_findings.section: PDF page 4; Representation of the Parser State
key_findings.qualification: Paper-reported qualitative comparison only; insufficient evidence to rank contemporary encoders or explain the contribution of attention. No numerical attention ablation is reported either.

limitations: Transfer-span evidence only: biomedical NER does not evaluate Topic identity, business email, asynchronous interleaving, or cross-message assignments (F01, F11; topic02.evaluated_tasks).

The transition system has local stack construction and destructive completion. Arbitrary shared-span combinations are not established as representable; no oracle coverage or complete constraint specification is reported (F02, F06).
Multi-overlap development failures, small category populations, and category-specific model reversals limit broad overlap claims (F05–F06).
Table 1 has unresolved headline-versus-breakdown counts on all datasets. Preserve the exact conflicting denominators (F07; topic02.material_inconsistencies).

Only one entity type is evaluated per dataset. Optional COMPLETE-y does not demonstrate multiple type labels for an identical span or work-Topic membership prediction (PDF page 3, Model; raw lines 288–292).

No standalone continuous-only full-test F1, noninferiority test, seed variance, confidence interval, or significance test is supplied. Full-test gains and Figure 4 development recall qualify the no-sacrifice claim (F03, F10).

Original annotation staffing, adjudication, IAA, duplicate controls, patient/author separation, and ShARe cross-corpus overlap are not reported in this paper; lack of a leakage audit is not proof of leakage (topic02.split_and_leakage).

No optimizer, learning rate, hidden dimensions, training-seed list, full oracle action-generation procedure, hardware throughput, or resource measurements are specified in the paper. BERT and attention claims lack controlled numeric ablations (F12; Sections 3–7).
NER gold can omit severity indicators. The paper gives qualitative extraction errors but no decision-scope preservation evaluation (F09, F11).

confidence_semantics: Confidence that the analysis accurately represents the frozen source and its evidence status, not the probability of successful msgloom transfer.
raw_claims: SHIFT moves the first token from the buffer to the stack; it implies this token is part of an entity mention.
REDUCE pops the top two spans s0 and s1 from the stack and concatenates them as a new span which is then pushed back to the stack.
RIGHT-REDUCE is the same as LEFT- REDUCE, except that s0 is kept in the stack.

evaluated_tasks.paper_task: Within-sentence exact biomedical entity mention extraction, including continuous, discontinuous, and overlapping mention structures. ShARe 14 annotations are repurposed for NER rather than its original disorder-attribute template-filling task.

annotation_unit.unit: A biomedical entity mention represented by a span or separated component spans over sentence tokens. Different mention instances can share tokens.
annotation_unit.concept_semantics: CADEC ADE annotations only; ShARe Disorder spans map to concepts in the SNOMED-CT disorder semantic group.
annotation_unit.scope: Not an annotation of sentences, clauses, EDUs, complete messages, or work-matter clusters as Topics.

prediction_unit.unit: An action sequence producing a collection of token spans/components as entity mentions for a sentence.
prediction_unit.complete_y: The paper proposes extending COMPLETE to COMPLETE-y for an entity type y; the experiments do not demonstrate that extension across multiple types.
prediction_unit.uncertainty: The decoder selects the most likely valid action. No calibrated membership uncertainty, abstention, or retained alternative Topic assignment is evaluated.

contiguity.gold: A mention may be continuous or consist of separated ordered components; mention instances need not partition all tokens.
contiguity.prediction: The transition parser can output both continuous and discontinuous mentions with some shared components.
contiguity.non_sequential_cluster: No non-sequential message/conversation cluster, cross-message identity, or thread-level Topic sequence is modeled or evaluated.

gold.mention_memberships_per_token: Can exceed one: Figure 1 shares muscle between two mention instances. Table 1 characterizes shared components. No maximum token-membership cardinality distribution is reported.
gold.multiple_types_on_same_exact_span: Not demonstrated in the selected evaluation annotations.

prediction.entity_types_in_each_test: One selected entity type per dataset.
prediction.mention_memberships_per_token: Multiple predicted mention instances can reuse a component through LEFT-REDUCE or RIGHT-REDUCE. Some shared-membership recovery is demonstrated; arbitrary cardinalities are not tested.
prediction.multiple_types_on_same_exact_span: Not evaluated; COMPLETE-y would assign type y to an emitted mention, not by itself demonstrate a set of labels for an identical span.

gold.one_semantic_object: Multiple separated components belong to one biomedical mention. Gold component counts appear in Table 1, with unresolved denominators.
gold.within_one_message: Sentence-local text in patient posts or clinical notes; within-email-message discontinuity is not directly evaluated.
gold.thread_level: Not annotated or evaluated as a thread-level Topic.

prediction.one_semantic_object: REDUCE can combine spans separated by intervening tokens into one mention. Table 3 right panel measures exact discontinuous mentions.
prediction.within_one_message: Demonstrated within source sentences, not an email message task.

overlap.gold_status: Present in the annotation targets: no, left, right, and multiple overlap categories; continuous mentions may also overlap.
overlap.predicted_status: Predicted and evaluated, not gold-only. Success differs by dataset/category; multi-overlap remains an evaluated failure on two development datasets, absent on the third.
overlap.scope: Shared token components between biomedical mention instances within sentences. Not shared Topics across messages, and not merely wholly nested mentions.
overlap.definition: Left/right refer to the position of a shared component in a discontinuous mention. Multi-overlap shares multiple components with other mentions and can form crossing compositions.
overlap.unsupported: Arbitrary crossing combinations, unrestricted membership cardinality, multi-type exact-span assignment, and email Topic overlap are not established.

metrics.reported_definition: Micro-average strict match mention F1; Table 2 also reports precision and recall.
metrics.operational_reading: Strict mention matching requires the predicted mention components to match a gold mention, with the selected entity type fixed per dataset. Standard micro P = correct predicted mentions / predicted mentions, R = correct predicted mentions / gold mentions, F1 = 2PR/(P+R). The paper names the metric but does not provide executable matching/filtering rules or all raw denominators.

RQ1.assessment: Supports examining component spans, but supplies no sentence/clause/EDU/hybrid comparison and permits clinically intentional severity exclusion.

RQ2.assessment: No email clusters, thread interleaving, or non-sequential message Topic identity task.

RQ3.assessment: Shared token membership and one mention with separated components are present in gold and some predictions. Entity-type cardinality and work-Topic cardinality are separate.

RQ4.assessment: Useful action-based construction and overlap-category failures; no universal expressivity result.

RQ5.strength: Risk evidence, no direct work-scope measurement
RQ5.assessment: Severity omission and malformed mention examples motivate preservation checks; downstream value is asserted, not measured.

interpretation.statement: A set of source-anchored component spans with shared membership is a candidate representation to test for Topic evidence. Biomedical mention identity is not Topic identity, and these NER scores cannot select a Topic architecture.

The described decoder consumes the buffer in order, combines only the top two stack spans, and retains at most one reduction operand; COMPLETE removes a span from the stack. No explicit split, arbitrary-span copy, or revisit action is supplied. These construction restrictions matter for crossing shared components. Unambiguous action-to-mention decoding does not imply mention-to-action coverage. The paper supplies neither an oracle coverage measure nor a proof that every gold structure is encodable, so multi-overlap failures must not be attributed solely to training sparsity. Exact unreachable structures should be determined by an oracle audit rather than inferred from F1 alone.

Separable component spans can preserve exact provenance while still excluding critical text. The left-atrium example shows why a flexible representation and decision-scope completeness require different validation.

The proposed nested-NER reinterpretation adds Body Location and General Feeling types and a covering ADE span. The paper does not evaluate a reversible recovery of original component-to-mention combinations under this reinterpretation. It is not evidence that bounding-span or nesting conversion preserves Topic membership.

Selecting only sentences with gold discontinuity makes a different evaluation population. Report all-mention and discontinuous-only results together, and label development diagnostics clearly. A dominant easy population can conceal failures on rare shared structures.

proposed_experiments.status: Untested msgloom research proposal; not architecture approval
proposed_experiments.proposal: Construct a small synthetic, source-anchored gold set with no/left/right/multiple overlap, crossing combinations, and separated components. Audit whether each gold assignment can be encoded and decoded without loss before training. Record unencodable, ambiguously decoded, and predicted-incorrect cases separately.
proposed_experiments.comparison: Compare a transition action encoding, contiguous covering spans, and explicit component sets. Include identical spans assigned to several Topic IDs independently of entity-type labels.
proposed_experiments.metrics: Exact gold-structure round-trip coverage and membership recovery; state the number of gold structures by category. Then measure model span/membership errors separately.

proposed_experiments.status: Untested msgloom research proposal; not architecture approval
proposed_experiments.proposal: Annotate synthetic work messages where a condition, negation, exception, supporting evidence, or approval/reply/action scope lies between or beside candidate Topic spans. Compare sentence, clause, span, EDU, and hybrid units using the same source text and gold work-matter identities.
proposed_experiments.metrics: Decision-bearing gold-unit recall, omitted-scope rate, broadened-scope rate, and reviewer-rated decision equivalence. Report exact span F1 separately. Retain ambiguous membership cases rather than force one assignment.

proposed_experiments.proposal: Evaluate all messages and explicitly labeled multi-Topic, overlapping, and discontinuous subsets. Separate within-message component assignment from cross-message Topic linking. Freeze document/thread/source-grouped splits and audit duplicate leakage before model comparison.
proposed_experiments.metrics: Task-specific span and membership P/R/F1, whole-message multi-label metrics, cross-message cluster metrics, and preservation metrics with separate gold/prediction counts. Measure overlap categories and report confidence intervals; do not pool incompatible denominators.
